newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan parliament committee OK's BOJ law reform.
newsitem.headline: Japan parliament committee OK's BOJ law reform.

text.p: A key committee of Japan's Lower House of parliament passed bills on Wednesday to revise a decades-old law and give the Bank of Japan (BOJ) more independence, officials said.

The bills, which aim to free the central bank from the grip of the once-powerful Finance Ministry, will be voted on by a full session of the Lower House on Thursday and then sent to the Upper House for approval, parliamentary officials said.
The BOJ law revision is part of deregulation promoted by Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto.

Hashimoto, himself a former finance minister, hopes to reduce the authority of MOF, which has come under fire for its handling of Japan's banking crisis and various embarrassing scandals involving its senior officials.
The plan calls for a number of changes to give more freedom to the central bank in deciding the nation's monetary policy:
-- The government could only ask the BOJ's policy-making board to postpone monetary policy decisions, while at present it can order the central bank to do so.
-- Two government representatives who are currently members of the BOJ's policy-making board could attend meetings "only when necessary".
-- The finance minister would continue to approve BOJ budgets, but only for costs other than those relating to money supply and monetary policy.
-- The minister would no longer have the authority to directly carry out inspections of the BOJ. Any checks on whether the BOJ has broken any laws or regulations would be made by BOJ auditors.
